question: What has OIG found at the Columbia VA?

no_form.answer:
OIG has published **14 reports** on the VA Columbia Missouri Healthcare System (station 589A4, Harry S. Truman Memorial Veterans' Hospital), from 2001 to 2026. They contain **73 recommendations**, and **1 is still open**. The data is current as of **November 4, 2026** (13 days old, not stale).

## The one open recommendation
**[Report 26-00046-284](https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/healthcare-facility-inspection/healthcare-facility-inspection-va-columbia-missouri)**, Healthcare Facility Inspection, published Oct 5, 2026. OIG was on site Feb 10–12, 2026, and made one recommendation:
> "Facility leaders take appropriate actions so staff maintain a safe and clean environment, in accordance with Veterans Health Administration Directive 1608(1), Comprehensive Environment of Care Program."

## Main recent findings (all closed as implemented)
**[Report 23-00112-161](https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/comprehensive-healthcare-inspection-program/comprehensive-healthcare-inspection-harry-s-0)**, Comprehensive Healthcare Inspection, May 2024. 7 recommendations, closed in 2024:
- Ongoing Professional Practice Evaluations for licensed independent practitioners were not done regularly and lacked service-specific criteria. The Clinical Executive Board also wasn't reviewing that data.
- Over-the-door alarms on mental health inpatient sleeping rooms weren't tested according to the manufacturer's instructions.
- Suicide prevention gaps: Comprehensive Suicide Risk Evaluations weren't always done the same day after a positive screen. Coordinators weren't doing at least five outreach activities a month. The suicide prevention team wasn't always notified when patients reported suicidal behaviors.

**[Report 20-01521-48](https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/hotline-healthcare-inspection/deficiencies-inpatient-mental-health-care-coordination-and)**, Hotline inspection, Jan 2021: *Deficiencies in Inpatient Mental Health Care Coordination and Processes Prior to a Patient's Death by Suicide.* 7 recommendations, closed in 2021:
- Better collaboration between the inpatient mental health unit and Vet Center staff.
- Safety plans that ask patients directly about access to lethal means.
- Communicating suicide risk at patient hand-offs.
- Assigning a Mental Health Treatment Coordinator.
- Accurate issue briefs.
- A review of whether an institutional disclosure was needed.
- One recommendation was for VA nationally: including Vet Center staff in root cause analyses.

**[Report 19-06864-183](https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/comprehensive-healthcare-inspection-program/comprehensive-healthcare-inspection-harry-s)**, Comprehensive Healthcare Inspection, July 2020. 14 recommendations, closed 2020–2021. Topics included:
- Utilization management documentation and reviews
- Root cause analyses
- Practitioner evaluations and exit reviews
- Long-term opioid therapy: risk assessments, urine drug testing, informed consent, and follow-up
- Annual suicide prevention training

## Repeat finding
OIG made the same recommendation in two reports, in 2017 and 2020: physician utilization management advisors were not consistently recording their decisions in the national database. Both are closed as implemented. OIG inspects against a standard checklist, so a repeat means the issue was cited again, not that nothing was done in between.

## Older reports
- [16-00550-145](https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/comprehensive-healthcare-inspection-program/clinical-assessment-program-review-harry-s) (2017, 13 recommendations)
- [13-03424-74](https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/comprehensive-healthcare-inspection-program/community-based-outpatient-clinic-and-primary-9) (2014, 13 recommendations)
- [13-03650-53](https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/comprehensive-healthcare-inspection-program/combined-assessment-program-review-harry-s-3) (2014, 18 recommendations)

Seven more reports from 2001–2015 have no recommendations in the data. They include hotline reviews:
- [05-01372-60](https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/hotline-healthcare-inspection/healthcare-inspection-alleged-suspicious-death-delay-surgery): alleged suspicious death and delayed surgery, 2006
- [11-04228-72](https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/hotline-healthcare-inspection/healthcare-inspection-discharge-travel-and-treatment-issues): discharge, travel, and treatment issues, 2012
- [14-01698-176](https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/hotline-healthcare-inspection/healthcare-inspection-follow-facility-response-administrative): follow-up on an administrative board of investigation, 2015

## Next inspection (estimate only)
OIG does not publish an inspection schedule. My **estimate is around February 2029**. It's based on the end date of the last inspection plus OIG's stated cycle of about three years. It is not an OIG date.

## Notes
- The facility is listed as VISN 15, but that label comes from OIG's tags, which mostly use VA's former numbering. It may not match the facility's network under the five networks VA created on July 15, 2026.
- I've summarized 25 of the 73 recommendations here; the rest are from the older reports. These are records only, not a rating of the facility.
